title: Object Pronoun Combinations
description: Combine direct and indirect object pronouns into single words (se lo, te lo, me la).

grammar.title: Object Pronoun Combinations (DO + IO in One Word)
grammar.content:
When you want to replace BOTH a direct and indirect object with pronouns, they combine into a SINGLE word. The indirect object pronoun (le/les) ALWAYS comes first, followed by the direct object pronoun (lo/la/los/las).

When le or les is followed by lo, la, los, or las, they change to SE + DO pronoun. This is one of the most important rules in Spanish pronoun usage.

Combinations:
- me + lo = melo
- me + la = mela
- te + lo = telo
- te + la = tela
- le + lo → se lo
- le + la → se la
- les + lo → se lo
- les + la → se la
- nos + lo = noslo
- os + lo = oslo (Spain only)

Placement rules:
- BEFORE conjugated verb: 'Te lo doy.' (I give it to you.)
- ATTACHED to infinitive: 'Voy a dártelo.' (I'm going to give it to you.)
- ATTACHED to gerund: 'Estoy preparándolo.' (I'm preparing it.)

When attached to an infinitive or gerund, add an accent mark to maintain proper stress.
examples: ¿Me lo puedes prestar? (Can you lend it to me?)
Se la recomendé al médico. (I recommended it to the doctor.)
Te lo voy a decir ahora mismo. (I'm going to tell it to you right now.)
Nos los compró en el mercado. (He bought them for us at the market.)
grammar.aid_note: Romanian combines object pronouns similarly: 'mi-l' (it to me), 'ți-l' (it to you), 'i-l' (it to him/her). Spanish 'se lo' is equivalent to Romanian 'i-l'. The Romanian system is actually more similar to English word-for-word than Spanish.

pronunciation.title: Accent Marks with Attached Pronouns
pronunciation.content:
When object pronouns are attached to an infinitive or gerund, an accent mark is often needed to maintain the original stress:

- dar + lo = darlo (2 syllables, stress on da) — no accent needed
- dar + te + lo = dártelo (3 syllables) — accent on the 'a' to maintain stress
- explicar + lo = explicarlo (4 syllables, stress on pa) — no accent needed
- explicando + lo = explicándolo (5 syllables) — accent on the 'a' to maintain stress
- preparar + lo = prepararlo (4 syllables, stress on pa) — no accent needed
- preparando + lo = preparándolo (5 syllables) — accent on the 'a'

The rule: if attaching pronouns pushes the stress to break the natural pattern, add an accent mark.
pronunciation.aid_note: Romanian pronouns are separated by a hyphen (mi-l, îți-l), while Spanish fuses them into a single word. The accent mark rules in Spanish are more complex due to the fused form.

exercises.question: What does 'se lo' replace in Spanish?
exercises.explanation: 'Se lo' replaces 'le/les + lo/la/los/las'. When le/les comes before lo/la/los/las, it changes to 'se'.

exercises.question: Complete: 'Yo ____ (dar) el libro a María. → Yo ____ lo doy.' (I give the book to María → I give it to her.)
exercises.explanation: 'Se lo doy' — 'le' changes to 'se' when followed by 'lo': le + lo = se lo.

exercises.question: Complete: 'Voy a ____ (decir) la verdad a ti. → Voy a ____ decir.' (I'm going to tell it to you.)
exercises.explanation: 'Decírtelo' — pronouns attach to the infinitive: te + lo + decir → decírtelo. An accent is added to maintain the stress.

exercises.question: Where do object pronouns go with a conjugated verb?
options: At the end of the sentence
They don't go with conjugated verbs
exercises.explanation: Object pronouns go BEFORE the conjugated verb: 'Te lo doy' (I give it to you).

exercises.question: Complete: '¿Me ____ (you) ____ (lo) ____ (decir)?' (Can you tell it to me?)
exercises.explanation: '¿Me lo puedes decir?' — pronouns go before the conjugated verb: me lo + puedes decir. Or with infinitive: ¿Puedes decírmelo? Both are correct.

exercises.question: Match each object pronoun combination with its English meaning:
exercises.explanation: Pronoun combinations: IO comes first, then DO. When le/les is before lo/la/los/las, it changes to 'se'.
